title: One normal Google credential interaction reaches the portal, Kanban and Carbon; first-use consent and policy reauthentication are reported separately.
Unknown identities, wrong companies, forged headers, wrong audiences, unauthorized service accounts and revoked memberships receive no data.
Row security hides unauthorized documents, other companies and revoked bindings under the real read role.
A same-input deployment is a no-op and a single-unit edit leaves every other unit, the migration ledger and database uptime untouched.
Authorized exact and lexical lookups on the warm path stay under the p95 budget in the local database; IAP/HTTP timing is reported separately.
Uncached lexical reads stay under the p95 budget on the cold local path.
Document answers show first evidence within 2 s and complete within 5 s at p95 on the standard query set.
Workforce verification plus cache policy revalidation stays under 50 ms at p95 in-process, excluding the external IAP boundary.
Measured IAP overhead remains part of the end-to-end targets.
Authorized Recall@10 for known-item queries over the labelled 500-question fixture.
No confident selection when the receipt or manual fixture is intentionally ambiguous.
Every generated claim cites delivered evidence; fabricated, conflicting and unsupported cases abstain.
Hidden matches change no counts or snippets, cache keys isolate actor/company/caller, poisoned entries are refused and telemetry carries no content.
A warm cache hit is denied as soon as policy is revoked.
Canonical user deactivation stops authorized reads within 30 s on the local read path.
New content is searchable within 60 s of extraction and deletion or local ACL revocation invalidates it within 30 s.
Re-extraction preserves accepted corrections and identical bytes keep separate source ACLs.
Ingest and review roles cannot execute business mutators or write ERP transactions.
A ticket command is executable only when complete, hash-matched and unambiguous, with a canonical idempotency identity.
A permitted ticket command creates exactly one ticket on the correct board/initial column with actor, deadline and audit metadata.
A command intent never executes retrieval or a mutation through the read transport, and the query contract rejects action fields.
The read transaction and read role cannot mutate portal or business tables.
Connectors share one authorization, version, pagination, freshness and deletion contract without changing the router.
